summary_expenses.title: IC card usage
summary_expenses.notes:
IC card total: 10,907 yen for two people.

This is the amount used for two people following this itinerary. 

We often opted to walk to attractions if they were close to each other.

Your final amount might vary depending on how often you use your IC card.

highlights.title: Hozenji Yokocho & Mossy Fudo Myoo
highlights.description: Just off Dotonbori, slip into this quiet stone-paved alley. Splash water on the moss-covered Mizukake Fudo statue for good luck and take atmospheric lantern photos at dusk.

highlights.title: Rikuro Ojisan Fluffy Cheesecake
highlights.description: Near Namba Station. Watch the bell ring every time a freshly baked, ultra-fluffy soufflé cheesecake comes out of the oven. Eat warm or save for your hotel room.

highlights.title: Kushikatsu Yaekatsu (Shinsekai)
highlights.description: The quintessential Osaka street snack in the shadow of Tsutenkaku Tower. Crispy skewered pork, lotus root, and quail eggs. Note: Strict no double-dipping rule in the shared sauce!

items.title: Shinsekai
items.how_to_access: Short walk from Shin-Imamiya Station (JR Osaka Loop) or Dobutsuen-mae Station (Midosuji Line).
highlights: View Tsutenkaku Tower (103m landmark)
Eat famous Osaka Kushikatsu (deep fried skewers) at Daruma or Yaekatsu
Experience the post-WWII retro Showa atmosphere and neon signs

items.title: Kuromon Market
items.address: 2 Chome Nipponbashi, Chuo Ward, Osaka, 542-0073, Japan
items.how_to_access: 2-minute walk from Nippombashi Station (Sennichimae / Sakaisuji Lines).
highlights: Sample fresh seafood skewers (grilled scallops, crab legs, uni)
Taste freshly prepared Kobe beef skewers and tamagoyaki
Pick up seasonal Japanese fruits (white strawberries, melon)
items.travel_tip: Bring cash as many traditional street food stalls do not take credit cards.

items.title: Shinsaibashi shopping street
items.how_to_access: Directly accessible from Shinsaibashi Subway Station (Midosuji Line).
highlights: Walk the 600-meter covered arcade lined with hundreds of fashion boutiques
Browse souvenirs, electronics, cosmetics, and confectionery
Explore adjoining cafes and nightlife venues

items.title: Try Street food in Dotonbori
items.how_to_access: Short 5-minute walk from JR Namba Station or Midosuji Line Shinsaibashi Station via Shinsaibashi-suji.
highlights: Compulsory photo snap with the Glico Running Man sign
Grab takoyaki street snack
Tonbori River 20-minute canal cruise
Stroll through the narrow atmospheric alleys of Hozenji Yokocho
items.travel_tip: Best experienced after sunset when neon billboards and glowing canal lights turn on.

highlights.title: Kogaryu Takoyaki in Triangle Park
highlights.description: Award-winning takoyaki topped with spicy mayonnaise and scallions in Amerikamura. Grab a boat and sit on the benches in Sankaku Koen (Triangle Park) like local Osaka youths.

highlights.title: Sunset Timing at Umeda Sky Building
highlights.description: Arrive at the Floating Garden Observatory 45 minutes before sunset. You get the 360-degree daylight view over Osaka Bay, the golden hour transition, and the glowing luminescent floor at night.

highlights.title: Hanshin Department Store B1 Snack Park
highlights.description: Famous standing food court under Umeda. Try authentic Osaka Ikayaki (chewy pressed squid crepe/pancake) for under ¥250.

items.user_notes: A discount chain with a Ferris wheel
items.how_to_access: Located right on Dotonbori canal, next to Tazaemon Bridge.
highlights: Ride the 77-meter yellow oval Ebisu Ferris wheel overlooking Dotonbori
Shop multiple floors of Japanese snacks, cosmetics, matchas, and duty-free goods

highlights: Ride the glass-encased escalator suspended between the two towers
Step onto the open-air circular roof deck on the 39th floor
Walk the Lumi Sky Walk path which glows in the dark at night

items.title: Osaka Castle
items.address: 1-1 Osakajo, Chuo Ward, Osaka, 540-0002, Japan

highlights: Climb to the 8th-floor observation deck for panoramic park views
Explore the 8-story museum detailing Toyotomi Hideyoshi's unification of Japan
Walk around the massive outer stone walls, moats, and Nishinomaru Garden

Admire the lion's mouth designed to swallow bad spirits

highlights.title: Okunoin Lantern Cemetery Night Walk
highlights.description: Walk the 2km path through 200,000 ancient stone memorials and towering cedar trees under stone lanterns after dark. Atmospheric, serene, and mystical.

highlights.title: Kadohama Goma-dofu (Sesame Tofu)
highlights.description: 1,200-year-old Koyasan specialty made from ground sesame seeds, mountain spring water, and arrowroot. Silky texture, eaten with freshly grated wasabi and dashi soy sauce.

highlights.title: Torodo (Hall of 10,000 Lanterns)
highlights.description: Located directly behind Kobo Daishi's mausoleum. Contains over 10,000 lanterns with two eternal flames said to have burned continuously for over 1,000 years.

highlights.title: Todai-ji Nigatsu-do Veranda
highlights.description: Climb up the wooden stairs behind the Great Buddha hall to Nigatsu-do. The elevated wooden balcony offers a free, panoramic view over the entire Nara basin with almost no crowds.

highlights.title: Nakatanidou Freshly Pounded Mochi Timing
highlights.description: High-speed mochitsuki hammering happens every 30-40 minutes outside the shop. Eat the warm yomogi (mugwort) mochi immediately while the dough is ultra-soft.

highlights.title: Kakinoha-zushi at Hiraso
highlights.description: Nara's historic sushi pressed and wrapped in persimmon leaves (which naturally preserves the mackerel and salmon). Perfect for a light lunch or to take on the train.

highlights.title: Kiyomizu-dera Autumn Night Light-Up
highlights.description: Mid-November features the special evening illumination. The wooden stage and red maple trees are lit against the dark sky, with a blue searchlight beam pointing toward Kyoto city.

highlights.title: Shirakawa Canal Walk
highlights.description: Walk along the Shirakawa River near Tatsumi Bridge at dusk. Far quieter and more romantic than Hanami-koji, with weeping willows and wooden teahouse reflections in the water.

highlights.title: % Arabica Kyoto Higashiyama
highlights.description: World-class espresso bar situated right on the cobbled hill facing Yasaka Pagoda (Hokan-ji). Perfect photo spot with Kyoto's most iconic silhouette.

highlights.title: Beat the Crowds at Bamboo Grove (Early Morning)
highlights.description: Tour groups arrive at Arashiyama by 8:30 AM. Arrive between 6:30 AM - 7:30 AM to have the majestic bamboo grove entirely to yourself for serene photographs.

highlights.title: Gio-ji Temple Moss Garden
highlights.description: A 15-minute walk past the main Arashiyama path. A tranquil thatched-roof hermitage surrounded by a lush carpet of moss, covered in fallen vibrant red maple leaves in mid-November.

highlights.title: Golden Pavilion Reflection at Kinkaku-ji
highlights.description: Best visited in the early afternoon when the sun directly hits the top floors, casting a mirror-like gold reflection onto Kyoko-chi (Mirror Pond).

highlights.title: Suirokaku Roman Aqueduct at Nanzen-ji
highlights.description: Hidden behind Nanzen-ji's main hall is a 19th-century red-brick Roman-style aqueduct. The contrast between ancient Japanese temple gardens and Western arched brick is stunning.

highlights.title: Blue Bottle Coffee Kyoto Machiya
highlights.description: A 100-year-old traditional two-story machiya townhouse converted into a serene, minimalist roastery just 3 minutes from Nanzen-ji.

highlights.title: Fushimi Inari Yotsutsuji Viewpoint
highlights.description: 90% of tourists stop at the lower torii loops. Keep ascending for 30 minutes to Yotsutsuji intersection for a soft drink, bench rest, and panoramic Kyoto skyline views.

highlights.title: Nodoguro (Blackthroat Seaperch) Kaisen-don
highlights.description: Kanazawa's most famous seasonal fish. At Omicho Market, get a kaisen-don (seafood bowl) with flame-seared fatty nodoguro seasoned with sea salt.

highlights.title: D.T. Suzuki Museum Water Mirror Garden
highlights.description: Designed by Yoshio Taniguchi. Sit quietly in the Contemplative Space Pavilion and gaze at the still water pool where periodic ripples break the stone reflections.

highlights.title: The Swimming Pool by Leandro Erlich
highlights.description: Inside the 21st Century Museum. Looking down from above is free, but stepping underground inside the pool requires a timed reservation ticket booked online on the museum website.

highlights.title: Kenrokuen Yukitsuri (Snow Ropes)
highlights.description: Mid-November is when gardeners raise the traditional conical rope arrays protecting centuries-old Karasaki pine branches from heavy snowfall. An iconic Japanese landscape.

highlights.title: Hakuichi Edible 24K Gold Leaf Soft Cream

highlights.title: Kanazawa Oden at Akatama or Miyoshi
highlights.description: Kanazawa consumes more oden than any other city in Japan. Warm up with baigai (sea snail), kuruma-fu (wheel-shaped wheat gluten), and soft daikon in clear golden dashi.

highlights.description: Skip the chaotic Takeshita Street after a quick peek and stroll Cat Street towards Shibuya. Trendy Japanese designer stores, quiet artisan cafes, and vintage denim.

transport_tips.title: IC Card (Suica / Pasmo)
transport_tips.detail: On iPhone: Wallet App -> '+' -> Transit Card -> 'Suica' -> Load via Apple Pay. Tap ticket gates directly without unlocking phone. Works for subways, city buses, vending machines, and convenience stores.

transport_tips.title: Shinkansen Luggage Rules
transport_tips.detail: Luggage with total dimensions (L+W+H) between 160cm and 250cm requires an oversized baggage seat reservation (rear row of car). Free when booking in advance via Smart-EX, but carries a ¥1,000 penalty if unreserved.

transport_tips.title: Luggage Forwarding (Takkyubin)
transport_tips.detail: Yamato Transport ('Black Cat') sends large suitcases hotel-to-hotel overnight for ~¥2,000-¥3,000. Forward main luggage from Kyoto to Tokyo and travel light with daypacks to Kanazawa & Takayama!

transport_tips.title: Cash vs. Card
transport_tips.detail: While cards and IC cards are widely accepted in Tokyo & Osaka, shrines, temples (goshuin stamps, entry fees), small ramen ticket vending machines, and Takayama morning markets are strictly cash (Yen) only. 7-Eleven ATMs accept international cards with zero ATM fee.
